styles.label: Beaches
styles.blurb: Cottesloe sunsets, Scarborough surf and Rottnest swims.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Kings Park, Swan Valley and day trips to Rottnest.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Northbridge eats, Fremantle seafood and coffee.

stays.why: Walk to Elizabeth Quay, Kings Park and the free CAT buses. Best base if you have no car.
Next to the CBD and the heart of late-night food and bars. Good value and lively.
Historic port with markets, seafood and the ferry to Rottnest. A relaxed base 30 min by train from the CBD.
Beachfront stays with surf, pools and sunset bars. About 20–30 min by bus or car to the CBD.

food: Try local seafood: fish and chips at Fremantle or Hillarys, and WA rock lobster when in season.
Coffee is a local obsession. Small roasters and cafés are everywhere in Northbridge and Fremantle.
Northbridge and the CBD have cheap Asian eats — noodles, dumplings and Vietnamese — often AUD 15–25 a meal.
Book ahead for popular weekend brunches and seafood dinners, especially in summer.
Perth is spread out and kitchens close early by big-city standards. Eat before 9pm on weeknights.
more_time: Take the ferry or a fast boat to Rottnest Island for a full day of beaches and quokkas; book tickets ahead.
Swap a city day for the Swan Valley: vineyards and breweries about 30–40 min by car or train plus bus.
Add a day trip to the Pinnacles Desert in Nambung National Park; it is a long drive, so a tour is easier.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the beaches, Kings Park and a full Rottnest day without rushing.

month_notes: January: hot and dry, highs near 30°C. Best for beaches; start outdoor plans early.
February: similar to January — hot, dry and busy with summer crowds.
March: still warm at about 28°C, with a few more rain days. Good beach weather.
April: mild and pleasant, highs near 25°C. A comfortable month for walking and day trips.
May: cooler at about 21°C with more rain. Pack a light jacket.
June: cool and wet — highs near 18°C and about 12 rain days. Plan indoor backups.
July: the wettest and coolest month, around 17°C. Bring a rain jacket.
August: still cool and showery, about 18°C. Watch the forecast for beach days.
September: warming to about 19°C with fewer rain days. Wildflowers start inland.
October: mild at about 22°C and drying out. A good shoulder month.
November: warm and mostly dry at about 25°C. Great for beaches and Rottnest.
December: hot and dry near 28°C. Book accommodation early for the holidays.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. Rain falls mostly from May to September.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Warm, dry days around 25–30°C. Ideal for beaches and Rottnest Island.

items.title: Wettest: June to August
items.text: About 12–15 rain days a month and highs near 17–18°C. Bring a rain jacket.

items.title: Mild shoulder months
items.text: April, May, September and October sit around 19–25°C — good for walking and day trips.

items.title: Sea breezes
items.text: The afternoon sea breeze is strong in summer. Mornings are calmer for the beach.

items.title: Strong sun
items.text: UV is high even on cooler days. Wear sunscreen and a hat.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and swimwear for summer; a warm layer and rain jacket for winter.

transit.best: Trains and the free CAT buses for the CBD; a car or tour for beaches and day trips.

modes.text: Transperth runs eight lines every 5–10 min at peak and about 15 min off-peak. Handy for Fremantle and the CBD.
Buses cover the CBD and suburbs. The CAT buses are free on five colour-coded routes.
A ferry links Elizabeth Quay to South Perth.
Uber and DiDi operate; taxis are Swan Taxis and Black and White.
Useful for beaches and day trips outside the train lines. Check parking in the CBD.
Easy in the CBD and Fremantle. The city is spread out, so use transport for longer hops.
